claims.text: R0123's profile lists research fields Bioinformatics, High-Performance Computing, Genomics and Cloud Computing, with keywords including read alignment, variant calling, pipeline parallelisation and cloud cost optimisation.
limitations: Profile self-description, not verified against project deliverables.

claims.text: R0123 is a participant in project SYN-PRJ-0254 (GENOMFLO), which develops a cloud-cost-aware orchestration layer that dynamically chooses between on-premises HPC and spot-instance cloud execution based on queue state, sample priority and real-time cloud pricing, plus containerised alignment and variant-calling workflow components.
limitations: Project summary describes planned pilot deployments at two regional clinical partners; no completed-deployment results are given in the evidence.

claims.text: R0123 co-authored work building a cost model for WGS alignment and variant-calling pipelines that combines hourly spot price distributions from two cloud providers, mean time to interruption, and checkpoint overhead for BWA-MEM2 and GATK stages; naive spot use without checkpointing increased effective cost 18–34% in high-volatility markets, whereas a bidding-and-checkpoint strategy cut cost 41% on average versus on-demand in stable price periods.
limitations: Modelled on WGS/WES cohorts at 10×–30× coverage, not on targeted short-read star-allele panels; transfer to a 24-sample panel batch is an assumption.
Pricing sampled over 90 days from two providers; results are sensitive to market volatility.

claims.text: R0123 co-authored a study on Snakemake/SLURM orchestration for GATK HaplotypeCaller, where genomic-interval scatter–gather reduced mean per-sample runtime from 4.1 hours to 41 minutes on 32 cores, with SNP precision 99.91%/recall 99.87% and indel precision 99.34%/recall 99.21% against the baseline on GIAB variants.
limitations: WES cohort at mean 85× coverage; the accuracy comparison is concordance with the authors' own baseline, not an independent clinical validation.

claims.text: R0123 has documented industry experience: a 2023 three-month consulting engagement with a Novi Sad health-tech startup auditing and optimising a cloud-based WES pipeline, reportedly reducing per-sample cloud spend by about 35%.
limitations: Self-reported profile field; no client reference, baseline figures or independent verification in the evidence.

claims.text: Because the company's bottlenecks are unprofiled but suspected in alignment and star-allele calling, R0123's combination of alignment-parallelisation work, scatter–gather throughput evaluation and spot/checkpoint cost modelling maps onto the primary levers likely needed to move from 9 EUR/sample toward below 3 EUR/sample.
limitations: Neither the company nor R0123 has measured this specific pipeline; mapping is by analogy from other WGS/WES pipelines.
Explicitly a hypothesis until per-step profiling is done.

claims.text: A first, bounded pilot: instrument the existing Snakemake pipeline to produce per-rule wall-time, CPU-hour and I/O profiles on two 24-sample batches, then build a per-sample cost model calibrated to the company's actual provider pricing and instance families, before any code optimisation.
limitations: Requires access to the company's cloud billing data and pipeline configuration, which are not in the evidence.
Cost-model outputs depend on provider price volatility during the pilot window.

claims.text: Targeted optimisation phase using interval scatter–gather and sample-level parallelism for the alignment and calling stages, plus checkpointed spot/preemptible execution guided by the cost model, with concordance against the current calls measured on retained clinical samples as the accuracy gate for the under-90-minute and sub-3-EUR goals.
limitations: Runtime and cost reductions reported in the cited studies were obtained on WGS/WES workloads, not on a targeted star-allele panel; gains may be smaller.
Effort assumes a 13-week pilot at the modest pace the proposer assigns, i.e. a 4-week plan, monitoring and a 4-week optimisation phase, with a 4-week accuracy-validation and handover period.
Spot-instance strategies carry interruption risk and require checkpointing to avoid cost regressions.

claims.text: R0123 participates in the GENOMFLO project (SYN-PRJ-0254) alongside other listed participants, and co-authored the cited publications with additional authors whose identities are unresolved in the source data; no assumption is made about those authors' affiliation or endorsement of this proposal.
limitations: Unresolved participant records mean co-author identities cannot be confirmed.
No affiliation or conflict-of-interest information beyond the profile is available.

claims.text: R0123's stated collaboration preferences are joint projects, contract research, consulting and student internships, and prefers partnerships with organisations facing concrete genomic cost or throughput constraints over theoretical or database-curation work.
limitations: Preferences are profile statements; actual availability, fees and any institutional IP constraints are not documented.

summary.text: R0123 is a strong technical match for C105-CH2: a bioinformatics/HPC researcher with registered evidence on cloud cost modelling for alignment and variant-calling pipelines, Snakemake scatter–gather throughput improvement with concordance checks, and a documented industry optimisation engagement, aligned with the company's unprofiled but suspected alignment/calling bottlenecks.

technicalRationale.text: The evidence covers the two likely levers: (a) cost-aware execution on spot/preemptible instances with checkpointing, and (b) parallelism/scatter–gather restructuring of alignment and calling stages, both with explicit accuracy-concordance measurements rather than speed alone.

Project GENOMFLO develops a cost-aware orchestration layer and containerised alignment/variant-calling components for laboratories with limited bioinformatics staff, which resembles the company's two-person bioinformatics setup.

cooperationScope.text: A time-boxed pilot (roughly 13 weeks) under contract research or consulting: a 4-week profiling and cost-model phase, a 4-week optimisation of alignment/calling parallelism and checkpointed spot execution, and a 4-week concordance validation and handover to the company's two bioinformatics staff.

validation.text: Acceptance gates: per-rule profile before/after, compute cost per sample measured against provider billing, total batch wall time, and star-allele call concordance versus the current pipeline on retained ethics-approved samples, with clinical accuracy treated as a non-negotiable constraint.
Concordance methodology should follow the cited practice of comparing against the existing baseline with precision/recall style metrics, not just timing.

constraints.text: Reported cost and runtime gains derive from WGS/WES workloads and modelled spot markets; they are not guarantees for a targeted star-allele panel, and spot usage without checkpointing can increase effective cost.
Collaboration preferences support contract research, consulting and joint projects; availability, fees, IP and data-processing agreements are not documented and must be agreed separately.

unknowns.text: The company's actual per-step bottlenecks, instance types and billing detail are unmeasured, so the sub-3-EUR and under-90-minute targets remain untested hypotheses.
Identity of co-authors and co-participants on the cited records is partly unresolved in the source data; no conclusions are drawn about their roles.

findings.explanation: R0945 was ranked 3rd on lexical hits for 'batch', 'cost', 'per', 'total', 'serbian' but every registered content item concerns cost-of-quality (PAF/appraisal-failure) modelling and inspection policy in electronics contract manufacturing (E191, E108, E059, E063, E045, E034, E117, E014, E148, E112). Nothing in the evidence covers bioinformatics pipelines, short-read alignment, variant/star-allele calling, Snakemake, Python workflow optimisation, or cloud instance cost engineering. His open_to (E052) is explicitly scoped to electronics manufacturers and CoQ/PAF consulting, and his notes (E120) demand 12+ months of defect/rework records plus limited capacity before mid-2026. Any proposal that treats him as a compute-cost or pipeline-throughput contributor is unsupported by attributable evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable evidence from R0945 address genomic pipeline runtime, cloud instance cost, or workflow parallelisation rather than electronics quality-cost accounting?

findings.explanation: R1005 was ranked 4th on 'calling', 'batch', 'per sample', 'cost', 'hours'. His evidence is industrial microbiology/fermentation (Bacillus strain drift, metabolomics of broths, plasmid retention, seed-lot management) and only incidental short-read SNP calling for strain identity (E152/E089 at EUR 38 per isolate in 2017 prices), which is neither star-allele calling nor cloud cost optimisation of a Python/Snakemake pipeline. open_to (E070) and notes (E172) restrict him to fermentation/root-cause work and NTP companies with a fermentation step; he also reports limited availability (E172). He cannot be presented as addressing the 9 EUR/sample compute or 4-6h runtime problem.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any attributable R1005 evidence on reducing cloud compute cost or runtime for a clinical short-read allele-calling pipeline, as opposed to fermentation metabolomics?

findings.explanation: R0775 was ranked 5th because abstracts contain 'cutting', 'instances', 'per', 'cost', 'minutes'. All attributable content is 2D irregular nesting/cutting-plan optimisation for garment, textile and furniture manufacturing, plus a fabric-roll assignment patent (E068). Run-time and cost figures refer to nesting heuristics on polygon datasets, not to cloud compute for sequencing pipelines. open_to (E094) and notes (E047) restrict him to material-waste/nesting/CAD-CAM work with digitised pattern libraries, explicitly noting he is less suited to other kinds of projects. Material-yield savings do not transfer to the GenovaMed per-sample cloud bill.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable R0775 evidence concern sequencing data processing, cloud VM cost, or bioinformatics workflow parallelism rather than textile nesting?

findings.explanation: R0751 was ranked 8th on 'price', 'pricing', 'serbian', 'consumers', 'cost'. His whole evidence set concerns hospitality/tourism revenue management, hotel reference-price experiments, GDPR-constrained personalised hotel rates, rate scraping and agritourism pricing. There is no bioinformatics, sequencing, cloud infrastructure, or pipeline performance content. Pricing of hotel rooms is not pricing of cloud compute or of pharmacogenomic tests, and his notes (E185) target property-management/revenue-management software and booking datasets, not diagnostics companies.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any attributable R0751 evidence on cloud compute cost, genomic pipeline throughput, or diagnostic test pricing under constrained reimbursement?

findings.explanation: R0595's spot/preemptible-instance work (E031/E144) is a stochastic bidding model with synthetic 30-day price series and 22% cost reduction versus a fixed-bid baseline; her remaining evidence is cost-sensitive classification, threshold selection, feature-selection stability and clinical tabular ML (E103, E083, E115, E041, E183, E044). This is modelling-side support for spot bidding and possibly for star-allele call decision thresholds, but there is no evidence of pipeline parallelisation, BWA/GATK-class alignment tuning, Snakemake optimisation, or hands-on sequencing-data engineering; her open_to (E159) is scoped to classification/LIS/model-evaluation consulting. Additionally she is on sabbatical in spring 2026 with availability limited to research collaboration and short consulting (E006), while the challenge needs an engineering optimisation effort. Counter-evidence: she should not be cited as a substitute for a pipeline/HPC engineer.
findings.recheckQuestion: Beyond E031's synthetic spot-market model, what attributable evidence shows R0595 has actually optimised the runtime or per-sample cloud cost of a real sequencing pipeline?

findings.explanation: R0633 was ranked 7th on 'price', 'pricing', 'current', 'instances', 'margin'. His evidence is workload-dependent/queueing-theoretic pricing for make-to-order metalworking and sheet-metal job shops, revenue management in ERP/MES environments and learning-curve cost models (E174, E128, E179, E008, E011, E017, E074, E075, E178). Some queueing/backlog-elasticity and cost-model ideas are conceptually adjacent to spot-instance bidding, but there is nothing on bioinformatics, spot markets as such, alignment/variant calling, or clinical accuracy preservation. His notes (E069) target NTP Novi Sad manufacturing/ERP/supply-chain companies. Treating him as a pipeline cost engineer would be unsupported.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable R0633 evidence address cloud spot pricing or genomic data-processing pipelines, or only manufactured-job-shop pricing?

findings.explanation: R0781's only pipeline-throughput content is co-authorship (author position 1) on the GATK HaplotypeCaller scatter-gather/Snakemake study (E048); her first-authored work is Bayesian network structure learning on plant RNA-seq/proteomics (E165, E038, E055), scRNA reproducibility benchmarking (E099), and Serbian clinical relation extraction (E039). Her open_to (E175) is scoped to plant/agricultural omics and probabilistic graphical models, and her notes (E013) state she is less interested in applied software-development roles and offers an HPC cluster rather than cloud genomics experience. Counter-evidence: E048 demonstrates transferable WES throughput know-how (4.1h to 41min per sample with GIAB concordance), but her stated restrictions and non-genomics publication profile mean her expected engagement on a cost/throughput engineering task is weaker than a ranking based on shared-abstract matching implies. Also note the shared publication SYN-PUB-01614 is attributed to both R0123 (author 3, E082) and R0781 (author 1, E078) - it must not be counted twice as independent expertise.
findings.recheckQuestion: Will R0781 actually contribute to applied pipeline/speed engineering given her stated preference against applied software-development roles and her plant-omics open_to scope?

findings.explanation: Even for the strongest technical candidate R0123, the attributable evidence covers cloud spot cost modelling for WGS alignment/variant calling (E023/E177), a cloud/HPC orchestration layer project (E158), GATK scatter-gather throughput with Snakemake and GIAB concordance (E048), SV-breakpoint aligner benchmarking (E142), BAM soft-clip compression (E086) and cache-oblivious alignment layouts (E092). None of it addresses diplotype/star-allele (CYP2D6/CYP2C19) calling from targeted short-read panels, pharmacogene copy-number/phase resolution, ISO 15189 validation of a changed pipeline, or a <3 EUR per 24-sample-batch costing at GenovaMed's scale. Cost-optimisation magnitudes in the literature (41% spot reduction in stable periods, 18-34% penalty without checkpointing) also do not by themselves establish the 9 EUR to <3 EUR per sample target. Proposals must not claim clinical-accuracy preservation for star-allele calls on the basis of these records.
findings.recheckQuestion: What attributable evidence verifies any experience with star-allele/diplotype calling and its clinical validation, as distinct from generic variant calling or SV benchmarking?

findings.explanation: Complete restriction review: R0123 (E060/E088/E030) fits genomic-scale cost/throughput partnership and has one 2023 three-month audit with ~35% WES cloud-spend reduction - the only directly comparable prior engagement. R0781: plant/agricultural omics only, no formal industry employment (E090). R0945: electronics-only open_to, requires >=12 months defect/rework data, cannot accept broad academic-output IP assignment, capacity-limited until mid-2026 (E120). R1005: fermentation-only, limited availability H1 (E172). R0775: nesting/material-waste only, less suited to other project types (E047). R0595: classification/LIS scope, spring-2026 sabbatical, short engagements only (E006). R0633: manufacturing/ERP pricing scope; open to co-developing IP only where commercially promising (E069). R0751: hospitality tech/booking data, no engagements shorter than three months (E185). Where the Proposer's claims reference any candidate outside these stated scopes, the claim's participation premise is unverified.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which proposed engagements fall outside a candidate's stated open_to/notes scope or availability window, and how would that be reconciled?

findings.explanation: All content items were resolved to a candidate only via explicit author/inventor/participant bindings; no unattributedEvidenceIds exist in any of the eight bundles. However, each bundle carries multiple IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED diagnostics (other co-authors without internal researcher IDs), so the number of co-authors and co-author affiliations on these papers is only partially known, and the credited contribution of each candidate is fixed solely by author position (e.g. R0123 is often author 0 or 3; R0945 author 1-3; R1005 author 2). Author position alone does not establish that a candidate led the cost/throughput-relevant part of a paper. Conversely, no content was found that is attributed to a candidate without an identity binding.
findings.recheckQuestion: For each cited paper, does the candidate's author position and known role support the specific contribution being asserted, given unresolved co-author identities?

noCounterEvidenceFound: No unattributed content Evidence was found in any of the eight candidate bundles (unattributedEvidenceIds empty for R0123, R0781, R0945, R1005, R0775, R0595, R0633, R0751).
No identityFlags were raised on any of the eight candidates in the pool (identityFlags arrays empty).
No evidence was found that R0123's stated open_to/notes restrictions conflict with a genomic-scale cloud cost/throughput collaboration; his restrictions are compatible with the challenge.
No evidence was found of IP-assignment or data-access blockers for R0123; no such restriction appears in his registered profile evidence.

No counter-evidence was found showing that the specific runtime improvements reported in E048 (41 minutes per sample) or E023 (41% spot cost reduction in stable price periods) are invalid within their own stated experimental settings; the concern raised is transferability to star-allele panels and GenovaMed's scale, not internal validity.

No evidence was found in any bundle of prior work with pharmacogene (CYP2D6/CYP2C19) diplotype calling, so no candidate can be credited or discredited on that specific capability from registered evidence.

findings.explanation: C1 restates the profile's own /fields and /keywords lists (E065: Bioinformatics, HPC, Genomics, Cloud Computing; E077: read alignment, variant calling, pipeline parallelisation, cloud cost optimisation). It is labelled as a profile self-description and flagged in limitations as unverified against deliverables, which is the correct epistemic status: profile keywords alone are not evidence of performed work. The surrounding claims (C3/E023, C4/E048, C5/E030) carry the actual attributable content, so the draft does not rest the technical case on E065/E077 alone. No correction required beyond keeping the stated limitation.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any draft section treat the E065/E077 keyword lists as performed-work evidence rather than as a self-described profile?

findings.explanation: C2 describes SYN-PRJ-0254 (GENOMFLO) accurately: E158 states the project 'develops and validates' a cloud-cost-aware orchestration layer and that 'pilot deployments are planned at two regional clinical partners', and E071 confirms R0123 is a listed participant (role 'principal investigator'). The claim is worded in present/development terms and the limitations explicitly note that no completed-deployment results exist. The technicalRationale sentence linking GENOMFLO to the company's two-person bioinformatics setup is a resemblance statement, not a claim of validated deployment at scale, so it stays within the source. The draft does not claim that GENOMFLO results are transferable or delivered.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is GENOMFLO ever cited as a completed, validated deployment rather than a project under development with planned pilots?

findings.explanation: C3 reproduces E023 faithfully: cost model over 500 synthetic cohort scenarios (50–1000 samples, 10×–30× coverage), naive spot use without checkpointing raising effective cost 18–34% in high-volatility markets, and a bidding-plus-checkpoint strategy cutting cost 41% versus on-demand in stable periods, validated against billing records of a 200-sample pilot. The qualifications that matter are already present: C3 limitations note the WGS/WES coverage regime and market volatility, C8 limitations note the panel-vs-WES transfer assumption and interruption risk, and the run constraints section states that these figures 'are not guarantees for a targeted star-allele panel'. C3 does not assert that 41% alone closes the 9 EUR to <3 EUR (67%) gap; C7 correctly inserts a profiling and calibration phase as the first step. This is an honestly bounded inference rather than an overstated guarantee.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any claim or section present the 41% spot figure (or the 4.1h-to-41min figure) as a guaranteed outcome for GenovaMed's 24-sample star-allele batches?

findings.explanation: C4 matches E048 exactly (412 WES samples, mean 85×; scatter–gather reduced mean per-sample runtime 4.1 h to 41 min on 32 cores; SNP precision 99.91%/recall 99.87%, indel 99.34%/99.21% against baseline on GIAB variants) and E082 confirms R0123 is author index 3 on that paper. The draft does not upgrade the internal concordance check into independent clinical validation: C4 limitations say so explicitly, and the validation section proposes an accuracy gate measured against the company's own current calls on retained ethics-approved samples — which is the appropriate comparison for 'without touching clinical accuracy'. Note the 41-minute figure is stated for a 32-core configuration and 85× WES, so the sub-90-minute goal is stated as a target to be tested, not as achieved.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is the E048 concordance result ever described as clinical validation of star-allele calls, or used to assert the under-90-minute target as already met?

findings.explanation: C5 quotes E030 precisely, including the 'approximately 35%' hedge and the three-month 2023 engagement on a cloud-based WES pipeline. C5 is labelled kind 'fact' but its limitations correctly identify it as a self-reported profile field with no client reference, baseline figures or independent verification. That is the only registered evidence of a prior comparable commercial engagement in the selected bundle, and it is directly on the challenge's core need (cloud cost of a sequencing pipeline), so citing it is proper — provided it remains framed as self-reported and WES-scoped, which it is.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is the 35% figure presented anywhere as audited or guaranteed rather than a self-reported profile statement?

findings.explanation: C6 is honestly typed 'inference' and its limitations state that neither party has measured this pipeline and that the mapping is by analogy until per-step profiling is done; the unknowns section repeats that the sub-3-EUR and under-90-minute targets remain untested hypotheses. C7 begins with instrumentation and cost-model calibration before any code optimisation, which is the correct posture given the company has not profiled bottlenecks. C8's targeted optimisation phase cites E048 (scatter–gather, sample-level parallelism), E023 (checkpointed spot bidding) and E142 (aligner runtime/RAM trade-offs) as method sources rather than as validated results for panels. Mapping is by capability, and all transfer assumptions are disclosed.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the draft ever assert that the sub-3-EUR or under-90-minute targets have been demonstrated, rather than proposed as bounded hypotheses?

findings.explanation: C9 correctly notes unresolved co-author/co-participant identities and draws no conclusion about their affiliations or endorsement. R0123's own ID is bound through explicit relations: author index 0 on SYN-PUB-01615 (E021) and SYN-PUB-01617 (E005), author index 3 on SYN-PUB-01614 (E082), participant on SYN-PRJ-0254 (E071). The author positions are not used to claim lead authorship of the cost/throughput work; the cost-model paper is first-authored by R0123 and C3 does not overstate the role on the two co-authored papers. This matches Counter CE-10.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is any author position used to assert a specific technical contribution not supported by the abstract content?

findings.explanation: C10 quotes E088 (joint projects, contract research, consulting, student internships) and E060 (interest in partners facing concrete genomic cost/throughput constraints; not theoretical or database-curation work). Both conditions are satisfied by this challenge: GenovaMed is a genomic data processor with an explicit cost and turnaround problem, and the draft proposes time-boxed contract research/consulting, not a database-curation collaboration. The constraints section correctly separates 'preferences support' from undocumented availability, fees, IP terms and data-processing agreements. No availability or capacity is inferred upward from the profile. The Counter report found no restriction conflict for R0123, and nothing in the draft claims guaranteed availability.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the draft infer availability, fees or IP terms beyond what E060/E088/E030 state, or propose an engagement form outside the listed open_to categories?

findings.explanation: The draft correctly centers on R0123 as the pair under review. The remaining pool candidates do not offer registered content on sequencing pipeline cost or star-allele calling: R0945 (electronics CoQ, E111/E191/E120 open_to electronics-only), R1005 (fermentation microbiology, E070/E172), R0775 (textile nesting, E047/E094/E068), R0751 (hospitality pricing, E185/E119), R0633 (job-shop pricing, E069/E026), R0781 (plant-omics/Bayesian networks, E175/E013), R0595 (clinical tabular ML plus a synthetic-price-spot model, E031/E159). Nothing in the draft borrows support from a different partner or proposes work outside the fixed pool. The absence of a candidate with pharmacogene diplotype calling (Counter CE-08) is a pool-level gap, not a defect in this pair's proposal, and does not by itself defeat cooperation suitability because the challenge's stated need is cost and runtime optimisation of an existing, correctly functioning pipeline rather than rebuilding calling accuracy.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any section attribute technical support to a researcher other than the selected partner R0123, or otherwise rely on evidence outside the fixed pool?

claims.text: R0123's profile lists research fields Bioinformatics, High-Performance Computing, Genomics and Cloud Computing, with keywords including read alignment, variant calling, pipeline parallelisation and cloud cost optimisation.
limitations: Profile self-description, not verified against project deliverables.

claims.text: R0123 is a participant in project SYN-PRJ-0254 (GENOMFLO), which develops a cloud-cost-aware orchestration layer that dynamically chooses between on-premises HPC and spot-instance cloud execution based on queue state, sample priority and real-time cloud pricing, plus containerised alignment and variant-calling workflow components.
limitations: Project summary describes planned pilot deployments at two regional clinical partners; no completed-deployment results are given in the evidence.

claims.text: R0123 co-authored work building a cost model for WGS alignment and variant-calling pipelines that combines hourly spot price distributions from two cloud providers, mean time to interruption, and checkpoint overhead for BWA-MEM2 and GATK stages; naive spot use without checkpointing increased effective cost 18–34% in high-volatility markets, whereas a bidding-and-checkpoint strategy cut cost 41% on average versus on-demand in stable price periods.
limitations: Modelled on WGS/WES cohorts at 10×–30× coverage, not on targeted short-read star-allele panels; transfer to a 24-sample panel batch is an assumption.
Pricing sampled over 90 days from two providers; results are sensitive to market volatility.

claims.text: R0123 co-authored a study on Snakemake/SLURM orchestration for GATK HaplotypeCaller, where genomic-interval scatter–gather reduced mean per-sample runtime from 4.1 hours to 41 minutes on 32 cores, with SNP precision 99.91%/recall 99.87% and indel precision 99.34%/recall 99.21% against the baseline on GIAB variants.
limitations: WES cohort at mean 85× coverage; the accuracy comparison is concordance with the authors' own baseline, not an independent clinical validation.

claims.text: R0123 has documented industry experience: a 2023 three-month consulting engagement with a Novi Sad health-tech startup auditing and optimising a cloud-based WES pipeline, reportedly reducing per-sample cloud spend by about 35%.
limitations: Self-reported profile field; no client reference, baseline figures or independent verification in the evidence.

claims.text: Because the company's bottlenecks are unprofiled but suspected in alignment and star-allele calling, R0123's combination of alignment-parallelisation work, scatter–gather throughput evaluation and spot/checkpoint cost modelling maps onto the primary levers likely needed to move from 9 EUR/sample toward below 3 EUR/sample.
limitations: Neither the company nor R0123 has measured this specific pipeline; mapping is by analogy from other WGS/WES pipelines.
Explicitly a hypothesis until per-step profiling is done.

claims.text: A first, bounded pilot: instrument the existing Snakemake pipeline to produce per-rule wall-time, CPU-hour and I/O profiles on two 24-sample batches, then build a per-sample cost model calibrated to the company's actual provider pricing and instance families, before any code optimisation.
limitations: Requires access to the company's cloud billing data and pipeline configuration, which are not in the evidence.
Cost-model outputs depend on provider price volatility during the pilot window.

claims.text: Targeted optimisation phase using interval scatter–gather and sample-level parallelism for the alignment and calling stages, plus checkpointed spot/preemptible execution guided by the cost model, with concordance against the current calls measured on retained clinical samples as the accuracy gate for the under-90-minute and sub-3-EUR goals.
limitations: Runtime and cost reductions reported in the cited studies were obtained on WGS/WES workloads, not on a targeted star-allele panel; gains may be smaller.
Effort assumes a 13-week pilot at the modest pace the proposer assigns, i.e. a 4-week plan, monitoring and a 4-week optimisation phase, with a 4-week accuracy-validation and handover period.
Spot-instance strategies carry interruption risk and require checkpointing to avoid cost regressions.

claims.text: R0123 participates in the GENOMFLO project (SYN-PRJ-0254) alongside other listed participants, and co-authored the cited publications with additional authors whose identities are unresolved in the source data; no assumption is made about those authors' affiliation or endorsement of this proposal.
limitations: Unresolved participant records mean co-author identities cannot be confirmed.
No affiliation or conflict-of-interest information beyond the profile is available.

claims.text: R0123's stated collaboration preferences are joint projects, contract research, consulting and student internships, and prefers partnerships with organisations facing concrete genomic cost or throughput constraints over theoretical or database-curation work.
limitations: Preferences are profile statements; actual availability, fees and any institutional IP constraints are not documented.

summary.text: R0123 is a strong technical match for C105-CH2: a bioinformatics/HPC researcher with registered evidence on cloud cost modelling for alignment and variant-calling pipelines, Snakemake scatter–gather throughput improvement with concordance checks, and a documented industry optimisation engagement, aligned with the company's unprofiled but suspected alignment/calling bottlenecks.

technicalRationale.text: The evidence covers the two likely levers: (a) cost-aware execution on spot/preemptible instances with checkpointing, and (b) parallelism/scatter–gather restructuring of alignment and calling stages, both with explicit accuracy-concordance measurements rather than speed alone.

Project GENOMFLO develops a cost-aware orchestration layer and containerised alignment/variant-calling components for laboratories with limited bioinformatics staff, which resembles the company's two-person bioinformatics setup.

cooperationScope.text: A time-boxed pilot (roughly 13 weeks) under contract research or consulting: a 4-week profiling and cost-model phase, a 4-week optimisation of alignment/calling parallelism and checkpointed spot execution, and a 4-week concordance validation and handover to the company's two bioinformatics staff.

validation.text: Acceptance gates: per-rule profile before/after, compute cost per sample measured against provider billing, total batch wall time, and star-allele call concordance versus the current pipeline on retained ethics-approved samples, with clinical accuracy treated as a non-negotiable constraint.
Concordance methodology should follow the cited practice of comparing against the existing baseline with precision/recall style metrics, not just timing.

constraints.text: Reported cost and runtime gains derive from WGS/WES workloads and modelled spot markets; they are not guarantees for a targeted star-allele panel, and spot usage without checkpointing can increase effective cost.
Collaboration preferences support contract research, consulting and joint projects; availability, fees, IP and data-processing agreements are not documented and must be agreed separately.
